rationale: The profile is opaque (no source, no function data), so the table hedges toward universally safe, cheap transformations while capping the expensive ones; the sample is the Shootout 'hash' benchmark, which is typically a compact, loop-heavy, pointer-intensive driver where runtime overhead is the main hazard and code size is secondary. SUB and IGV get high security/diversity weights with near-zero cost/risk weights since arithmetic substitution is cheap and semantics-preserving, making them the workhorses; SPLIT is similar but with slightly lower security weight since it mainly amplifies other passes. BCF and IBR provide the strongest control-flow resistance, so they keep high gain weights, but their RuntimeCost weights are raised to ~0.5 so the selector spares hot loops inside hash-table lookups; FLA gets the highest SizeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights because flattening pointer/branch-dense code inflates size and can interact badly with indirect control flow; ICALL earns high security weight (indirect-call conversion strongly hinders static analysis) with moderate risk weight to account for calling-convention edge cases. Overall the table maximizes reverse-engineering resistance from low-cost passes while gating the high-overpass transformations behind per-function cost features.
